major_features: Custom binary wire protocol supporting framed message frames and multiplexed connection streams
Segmented append-only on-disk log storage with configurable byte-size and time-based rotation
Consumer group coordination engine implementing dynamic partition assignment and heartbeat liveness tracking
Explicit message acknowledgment (ACK) and negative acknowledgment (NACK) offset tracking loops
Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) diversion mechanism for messages exceeding maximum delivery retry thresholds
Configurable message retention policy enforcing background disk compaction and segment pruning
Non-blocking TCP network server utilizing Java 21 Selector and SocketChannel multiplexing
Deterministic integration harness injecting network packet drops, socket delays, and disk full simulations
candidate_ideas.name: OmniStream MQ
candidate_ideas.pain: Developers building local-first event-driven pipelines lack lightweight brokers that support multiplexed consumer subscriptions, dead-letter queues, and deterministic message replay without heavy external runtimes.
candidate_ideas.problem: Traditional enterprise message queues require heavy external cluster management, while raw socket protocols lack consumer group balancing, acknowledgment persistence, and durability guarantees.
candidate_ideas.solution: A high-performance Java 21 broker implementing a binary wire protocol, zero-copy segment file I/O, consumer group rebalancing, and configurable retention policies entirely from scratch.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Systems Engineers and Distributed Infrastructure Architects
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic integration suite testing concurrent producers, consumer group partition handoffs, abrupt client disconnection recovery, and corrupted offset index repair using automated byte-injection scripts.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
